subject: bar magnet
title: What If You Cut a Magnet in Half?

scenes.text: What if you cut a magnet in half? You'd never get a lonely north pole.
Snap a bar magnet and both pieces instantly have a north and a south. Two new magnets.
Inside, billions of tiny regions called domains already point the same way. The break just exposes them.
Keep cutting, down to a single electron. It's still a tiny magnet with two poles.
A lone pole, a monopole, was predicted in the 1930s. In 1982 a Stanford detector saw one possible hit. Never again.
Want to really kill a magnet? Don't cut it. Heat iron past 770 degrees Celsius and the magnetism vanishes.

description:
What if you cut a magnet in half? Each piece becomes a complete magnet with its own north and south pole, because the magnetism comes from aligned domains and ultimately from electrons, which are tiny dipoles themselves.
No magnetic monopole has ever been confirmed; one candidate event at Stanford in 1982 was never repeated. Heating iron above its 770 C Curie point destroys its magnetism.
